summary:
The bakery puts its gable end to the street on a narrow plan. The ground storey is dark deepslate brick with a shop window and fold-down counter on each side of the door. Above it, a white half-timbered storey framed in stripped spruce juts out over the street, under a steep slate roof with a flour-loft hoist beam at its peak. A lower cobbled-deepslate bakehouse wing on the east holds the brick oven, which bulges out at the back under a tall red chimney. Narrow gable-to-street Germanic bakery: dark deepslate ground storey, jettied stripped-spruce Fachwerk upper storey with white wool daub, steep slate roof, hoist beam, and a cobbled-deepslate bakehouse wing with a brick barrel-vault oven under a smoking chimney.
Written: elements.md (checklist with constructions), and PALETTE (ids checked), VOCABULARY (41 helpers), ROOMS (6 with boxes), PARTS (6) and Notes appended to plan.md.
Stairs rise north in the SW corner from the Backstube to the Stube; the attic is reached by a ladder, and the oven has a hollow flue for its two campfires.

Warm, busy, scrubbed spruce floor, white daub. Keep the front door approach (11,2..3,10) and the wing doorway landing (15,2,15) free; stair housing x=7..8 z=14..15 is solid.

rooms.purpose: The baker's living room over the street: brick tile stove (one red accent), table set under the front windows, bookshelf and lectern, carpet rug, hanging lantern. Cosy daub and spruce. Keep the stair arrival (7..8,7,13) and the stair rail free.

rooms.purpose: Quiet bedroom at the back: red bed with the head to a wall under/near the back windows, chest at the foot, shelf, rug. Keep the stair rail at x=9 z=15..17 and the attic ladder column (9,7..11,20) with backing (9,7..10,21).

concept_subject: A traditional German town bakery seen from a gravel lane, its tall gable end facing the street. The ground storey is charcoal deepslate brick on a smooth darker plinth. The spruce front door, with a glass transom above it, is centred between two wide three-pane shop windows. Each window has a spruce-slab sales counter standing proud below it, with spruce shutters folded back beside it. A tan stripped-spruce beam runs across the whole front at lintel height, and five spruce brackets carry the upper storey, which juts one block out over the pavement. That storey is classic Fachwerk: stripped-spruce posts, sill and head beams, and a breast rail, filled with bright white panels and braced with darker spruce stairs in the end panels. Its two 2x2 windows have flower boxes of red tulips. The steep grey slate roof (dark tiles with lighter mottling, spruce barge boards) rises to a high ridge running back from the street. The front gable is timbered too, with a collar beam, a king post, two small attic windows and an open loft door with shutters. Above the loft door, a stripped-spruce hoist beam juts past the verge, with an iron chain and a dangling barrel. A wrought hanging sign reading "Bäckerei" swings on a spruce arm at the right corner, and lanterns hang under the overhang. Set back on the right is a lower single-storey cobbled-deepslate bakehouse wing with its own small slate gable. At its back, a red-brick bread oven with a barrel-vaulted top pushes out into the yard, and a slim brick chimney with a dark band rises from it, smoking, to about two-thirds of the main roof's height. Behind the house is a spruce-fenced yard with a stack of spruce firewood, barrels and hay bales, a little wheat patch, and two small spruce trees.
